html:
The Esk'etemc are a Secwépemc (Shuswap) community of central British Columbia, at Alkali Lake south of Williams Lake, near the Fraser River.

They lived by salmon fishing on the Fraser and by hunting and gathering on the plateau. Ranching and the 1860s Cariboo gold rush brought settlers onto their land, and children were sent to the St Joseph's Mission residential school. In the 1970s the community was known for very high rates of alcoholism. It then cut them sharply, led by its chief and his wife, and became a model for Indigenous sobriety movements across North America; a 1985 film, The Honour of All, told the story. Their neighbours included the Tsilhqot'in to the west and the Nlaka'pamux to the south.
sum: The Esk'etemc are a Secwépemc (Shuswap) community of central British Columbia, at Alkali Lake south of Williams Lake, near the Fraser River.
